title: OpenAI argues the useful metric is cost per completed outcome
friendlyTitle: The cheapest AI is not always the least expensive choice
summary: OpenAI set out a full-stack strategy for lowering the cost of useful intelligence through cheaper models, serving efficiency, routing and context management. It argues that buyers should measure the total cost of a successful result—including retries, oversight and errors—rather than token price alone.
friendlySummary: OpenAI says people should count the full cost of finishing a job, including mistakes, retries and human checking—not only token prices.
whyItMatters: This is a practical framework for buying and operating AI. A cheap model can be expensive if it needs repeated attempts, while a stronger model can save money when it reliably finishes the job.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This helps teams compare AI tools by real results instead of a price that tells only part of the story.
